 Ukraine conflict on November 21st: Could Ukraine be about to withdraw near Dobropillia?
 (Dan Tri Newspaper) - The Russian army is preparing to encircle Bilozerske, while Ukrainian forces stationed there appear to be on the verge of withdrawing from the town located north of Dobropillia.
 Báo Dân trí • 21/11/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e Add Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e 0 The fighting in Ukraine continues fiercely (Illustrative image: Skynews).
 Russia retaliates for Ukraine's attack on the Crimean bridge. 
 According to Rybar News, the Russian Armed Forces (RFAF) retaliated against Ukraine for collapsing the Crimean Bridge, and the capital Kyiv in particular, and Ukrainian territory in general, suffered attacks.
 Over the past 24 hours, Moscow's forces have carried out attacks on various targets using UAVs, cruise missiles, and ballistic missiles, focusing on energy and transportation infrastructure. 
 Russian warships launched Kalibr cruise missiles from the port of Novorossiysk during attacks on targets in Ukraine on the night of November 19-20 ( Video : Exilenova+).
 Several bridges in Kyiv were damaged but remained standing, while numerous facilities across central Ukraine suffered a series of attacks. Targets in the west were also attacked, and power outages were reported in Lviv and its surroundings, as well as in the Transcarpathia region.
 Conversely, the Ukrainian Armed Forces (AFU) launched more than 300 UAVs toward various areas of Russia. The majority of these were intercepted in areas near the front lines. Missile warnings were also issued in several other regions.
 The Military Summary channel claims that Moscow launched its largest airstrike since 2022. In just one night, 70 Kh-101 cruise missiles, 16 Kalibr missiles, 49 ballistic missiles, and 500 UAVs – all launched in three phases – rained down on Ukraine.
 Kyiv bore the brunt of the attack: five bridges over the Dnieper River were hit, with the South Bridge being closed in both directions. 
 On the night of November 19th and the early morning of November 20th, Russia launched a massive airstrike on Ukraine. The capital, Kyiv, suffered a fierce barrage of missiles (Photo: Military Summary).
 Ukraine deploys laser-based air defense system in Kyiv. 
 Ukraine has deployed its first laser-based air defense system to protect Kyiv from Russian UAVs. However, the weapon has yet to intercept any actual targets, so its effectiveness remains unproven, according to the Kyiv Independent.
 In early November, Carmine Sky deployed a new laser system called Blysk as part of Kyiv's air defense network. According to the company, the system is capable of burning through the armor of Geran UAVs in just seconds.
 Laser weapons could offer Ukraine a lower-cost way to counter UAV attacks, as they use only electricity instead of expensive interceptor missiles. However, accurately tracking targets with lasers could be challenging in the face of highly maneuverable UAVs.
 Ukraine's deployment of Blysk missiles comes amid the growing development of laser weapons as a cheaper alternative to traditional anti-aircraft missiles. This program, initiated by the Ukrainian Ministry of Defense , allows companies to establish air defense units operating under the command and control of the Ukrainian Air Force.
 Several notable developments on the ground. 
 You may also like News channels and war correspondents updated the developments on the front lines on November 20th. 
 On the Dnipropetrovsk front, Kyiv forces are launching an offensive north of Komar, with fighting ongoing between Yalta and Dachne. Small-scale clashes between groups of soldiers from both sides continue in the large "gray zone" between the Vovcha River and the regional border, according to the Rybar news agency. 
 The stalemate between Russia and Ukraine continues in the Dnipropetrovks region and the area bordering Zaporizhia province. The advantage is slightly tilted towards Kyiv's forces (Photo: Rybar).
 On the Zaporizhia side, the AFU continued to launch counterattacks near Mala Tokmachka and Novodanylivka. Orekhov and Novoandriivka were still under attack from Russian UAVs and fighter jets. The situation near Stepnohirsk remained essentially unchanged, while the Russian army made some tactical advances. 
 Map of the Russia-Ukraine conflict in Zaporizhia on November 20. The front is becoming increasingly intense due to the continuous counterattacks by Kyiv forces (Photo: Rybar).
 Field correspondent Evgeniy Lisitsyn also confirmed that Kyiv forces attempted to bypass RFAF positions near Orekhov. The Russian Ministry of Defense reported several attacks near Preobrazhenka and Kamyshevakha.
 In Dnipropetrovsk, Moscow forces reportedly repelled several counterattacks. The Russian Ministry of Defense noted an attack targeting Kyiv units near Kolomiitsi and Podhavrylivka.
 On the Dobropillia front, according to preliminary information, the RFAF has expanded its encirclement around Serhiivka from the south. The Russian Ministry of Defense reported attacks near Bilozerske. 
 Russian troops are encircling the town of Bilozerske north of Dobropillia, putting Ukrainian forces in a difficult position and even risking a retreat (Photo: Evgeniy Lisitsyn).
 In Konstantinovka, Moscow units have advanced to Mykolaipillia and are attempting to hold their positions in the southern suburbs. Additionally, the RFAF has made advances in Veroliubivka.
 Around Siversk, localized advances by Russian troops have been noted near Dibrova and Ozerne; however, neither side has yet gained complete control of the area.
 Reports indicate that the front line has shifted westward along the Zherebets River, while Moscow's forces remain in position south of the city of Liman. 
 Despite a fierce counterattack from Ukraine, Russian forces are holding their positions in southern Liman (Photo: Evgeniy Lisitsyn).
 Fighting was reported near Vilcha and Bilyi Kolodiaz in the Kharkiv region. The Russian Ministry of Defense reported attacks near Chuhuiv, while in Sumy, there were reports of AFU counterattacks near Sadky and Yunakivka. The Russian Ministry of Defense also recorded attacks near Yastrebine and Krovne. On the Kherson side, the RFAF launched intense shelling targeting villages on the left bank of the Dnipro River; casualties are being verified.
 The Russian Ministry of Defense reported attacks targeting Kyiv forces in the vicinity of the cities of Sloviansk and Kramatorsk.
 Ukraine is showing signs of preparing to withdraw from Bilozerske near Dobropillia. 
 You may also like According to the Readovka news site, Moscow units are preparing to encircle Bilozerske, while Kiev forces stationed there have begun showing signs of withdrawing from the town located north of Dobropillia.
 Specifically, the 51st RFAF Combined Arms Group has made significant advances in fighting near the town of Bilozerske. Russian assault units recently approached the village of Vesna via several dry stream beds. Fighting continues in this village and surrounding areas.
 Notably, the RFAF chose to bypass Bilozerske. This suggests that the Russian army's objective was likely not simply to pass through the town, but also to control the Svyatokovskaya and Novodonetskaya mining areas.
 However, at the present moment, another objective may become more important. Units of the RFAF 1st Army Group are continuing to exert pressure on the Novovodanoye and Zolotoy Kolodez areas. With Moscow's forces advancing towards the village of Vesna, Ukrainian units that were trying to pressure the Russian front lines near these settlements are now surrounded. In that situation, the AFU is forced to switch to a defensive posture. 
 Russian troops are expanding their foothold in the red zones, preparing to encircle the town of Bilozerske north of the city of Dobropillia (Photo: Readovka).
 RFAF control of the village of Vesna will pave the way for the operation to capture the village of Novopavlovka. This will create a solid foundation for an offensive towards the Novopokrovskaya mine, and also open up opportunities to exploit advantages in the Novodonetskaya mine area.
 It should be noted that the aforementioned technical facilities serve as the "northern gateway" into and out of Bilozerske. Without them, the Kiev forces stationed there would be at risk of being surrounded. This becomes even clearer now that Moscow's leading units are present in the Bilozerske mining area and the mining town of Bokovoe.
 Thus, the 51st Army Group of the RFAF is attempting to repeat the scenario previously applied to Kyiv's units stationed in Bilozerske and Dobropillia. While Ukrainian troops managed to withdraw from Belitsk earlier, it is unlikely they will be able to do the same in Bilozerske.
 The question is: will the Kyiv command hold out at Bilozerske until completely surrounded, or will they order their units to withdraw from the town if the situation worsens?
